questions.question:
Correct the following sentence.

One of the member of his family died due to a heart attack.
options: One of member from his family died of a heart attack.
One of the members of his family died due to a heart attack.
One of the members of him family died due to a heart attack.
One of the member of him family died due to a heart attack.
questions.solution:
The phrase 'one of the' is used to describe something/someone from the same group and it is always followed by a plural noun. So, the singular noun 'member' should be replaced by the plural noun 'members' in the given sentence. This is why the given sentence and options (a) and (d) are incorrect.

Option (c): 'his' instead of 'him' would be appropriate to refer to the family.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given.

She likes to made people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
options: She likes to makes people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
She likes to making people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
She likes to be make people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
She likes to make people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
questions.solution:
The infinitive marker 'To' is always followed by a base form of the verb, so the use of 'made/makes/making' [V2/V3, V5, V4 respectively] will be incorrect here. 'To + be' is followed by a participle form of the verb which is not the case in option (c) ['make' is the base verb], therefore, it will be incorrect as well. The grammatically correct sentence is mentioned in option (d).

The correct sentence is - 'She likes to make people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.'

Hence, option (d) is correct.

NOTE/-

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below: Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground. Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion. The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect. The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes completed action or state of the thing spoken of. A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n. One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given.

The infantry has taken the brunt of the missile attacks.
options: The infantry has been taken the brunt of the missile attacks.
The infantry have taken the brunt of the missile attacks.
The infantry is taking the brunt of the missile attacks.
The infantry was taken the brunt of the missile attacks.
questions.solution:
'Cattle, cavalry, poultry, children, gentry, infantry, police' are certain nouns that are singular in form but plural in meaning. They take plural verbs. The grammatically correct sentence is mentioned in option (b). 'Has, Is, and Was' are all plural verbs.

The correct sentence is - 'The infantry have taken the brunt of the missile attacks.'

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of adverb of frequency.
options: These girls are often late for work.
These girls get late for work due to the traffic.
These girls are late for work because of their laziness.
These girls got late yesterday for some unknown reason.
questions.solution:
Among the given options, option (a) contains the word 'often' which is an adverb of frequency. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Adverbs of frequency always describe how often something occurs, either in definite or indefinite terms.

Option (d) contains the adverb 'yesterday' which is the adverb of time.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in positive degree of comparison.

She is the most beautiful lady in the room.
options: She is more beautiful than others in the room.
The most beautiful lady in the room is she.
She looked very beautiful sitting in the room occupied by many other ladies.
In this room, of all the people, she is the most beautiful.
questions.solution:
The given sentence is already in the superlative degree of comparison. To convert it into a positive degree of comparison, we need to express the idea without comparing it to others.

Option (a) - This option maintains the comparative comparison, so it's not in the positive degree.

Option (b)- This option retains the superlative comparison, so it's not in the positive degree.

Option (c) - This option expresses the idea without comparing her beauty to others, which is characteristic of the positive degree.

Option (d)- This option doesn't properly convey the positive degree of comparison. It still includes a comparison.

Among the given options, only option (c) fully captures the positive degree of comparison. It presents the idea that her beauty stands alone and is not being compared to others. Therefore, the correct answer is (c).

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the positive degree of comparison.

She is the most patient person I know.
options: She is more patient than most people.
She is a very patient person.
She is the most patient person I know.
She is patient, but not the most patient.
questions.solution:
The original sentence is in the superlative degree, comparing her patience to others whom the speaker knows. The correct answer expresses the positive degree by stating that she is a very patient person without making any comparative or superlative comparisons.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Option (a) is in comparative degree.

Options (c) and (d) are in superlative degree.

Note:

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. An unexpected act of kindness can strengthen our relationships. It can be practised through an acts of generosity and empathy.

B. A unexpected act of kindness can strengthen our relationships. It can be practised through the acts of generosity and empathy.

C. An unexpected act of kindness can strengthen our relationships. It can be practised through acts of generosity and empathy.

D. The unexpected act of kindness can strengthen our relationships. It can be practised through a acts of generosity and empathy.
options: B
A
D
C
questions.solution:
The indefinite article 'an' should be used before 'unexpected' primarily because it has a vowel sound. Also, 'an' is referring to an unspecified noun in the sentence, that is, 'act'.

None of the articles is used before the noun 'acts' in the second sentence because it is a plural and unspecified noun.

The sentences A, B, and D depict grammatically incorrect usage of the articles.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. Recently, an documentary on Cold War was screened. It provided the comprehensive overview of that period.

B. Recently, the documentary on a Cold War was screened. It provided a comprehensive overview of that period.

C. Recently, a documentary on an Cold War was screened. It provided an comprehensive overview of that period.

D. Recently, a documentary on the Cold War was screened. It provided a comprehensive overview of period.
options: C
D
B
A
questions.solution:
The indefinite article 'a' should be used before 'documentary' because it is introducing an unspecified noun 'documentary'. Similarly, the indefinite article 'a' should also be used before 'comprehensive' because it refers to an unspecified and singular noun, that is, 'overview'. Also, since 'documentary' and 'comprehensive' are not vowel-sounding words, they cannot be preceded by 'an'.

The definite article 'the' should be used before 'Cold War' because it introduces a specific noun 'Cold War'.

No indefinite article is used before 'overview' because it is uncountable in nature.

The sentences A, B, and C depict grammatically incorrect usage of the articles.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer. Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a correct sentence?
options: Our marketing endeavours focus in building a deep emotional connection while creating an appreciation for platinum's unique qualities.
Our marketing endeavours focuses on building a deep emotional connection while creating an appreciation for platinum's unique qualities.
Our marketing endeavours focus on building a deep emotional connection since creating an appreciation for platinum's unique qualities.
Our marketing endeavours focus on building a deep emotional connection while creating an appreciation for platinum's unique qualities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (d) as it maintains a clear and coherent structure in expressing the focus of marketing endeavours.

Let us look at the incorrect options:

Option (a): The preposition "in" is incorrect; it should be "focus on building." Therefore, this option has a preposition error.

Option (b): There is a subject-verb agreement error in this option. The plural subject "Our marketing endeavours" should take the plural verb "focus," not the singular verb "focuses."

Option (c): The use of "since" is not suitable in this context. "Since" is used to express a cause or reason, but it doesn't appropriately connect the ideas in the sentence. Any conjunction like "while" is more fitting for expressing simultaneous actions.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in present tense form.

We received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
options: We will be receiving a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We have received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We had received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We were receiving a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
questions.solution:
The correct option that expresses the given sentence in present tense form is (b). Option (b) changes the verb "received" (past tense) to "have received" (present perfect tense). The present perfect tense is used to talk about actions that were completed at some unspecified time before the present moment and have relevance to the present. It is formed using the auxiliary verb "have" (or "has" for singular subjects) followed by the past participle of the main verb (in this case, "received"). Option (a) is in the future continuous tense ("will be" + present participle of the verb). Option (c) is in the past perfect tense ("had" + past participle of the verb). Option (d) is in the past continuous tense ("were"/ "was" + present participle of the verb). Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

The photocopier collated the documents for you.
The photocopier is collating the documents for you.

Option (b) is in the simple past tense, which is formed using the "second" form of the verb. Option (c) is in the present continuous tense, which is formed using "is" + the present participle of the verb. questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form.

We will have made the journey to Wales in five hours.
options: We have made the journey to Wales in five hours.
We make the journey to Wales in five hours.
We will make the journey to Wales in five hours.
We made the journey to Wales in five hours.
questions.solution:
The correct option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form is (d). Option (d) changes the verb phrase "will have made" (future perfect tense) to "made" (simple past tense). The simple past tense is used to describe actions or events that were completed in the past. The simple past tense is formed by using the past form of the main verb (made). Option (a) is in the present perfect tense, which is formed using "have" + past participle of the verb. Option (b) is in the simple present tense, which is formed using the base form of the verb (make).

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A. Fruits are a good source of vitamins. An healthy diet should include fruits.

B. Fruits are an good source of vitamins. A healthy diet should include fruits.

C. Fruits are a good source of vitamins. A healthy diet should include fruits.

D. Fruits are an good source of vitamins. An healthy diet should include fruits.
options: C
B
D
A
questions.solution:
Sentence C is grammatically correct. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

A - "An healthy" is incorrect because the indefinite article "an" is used before words starting with a vowel sound. "Healthy" starts with a consonant sound, so the definite article "a" should be used instead.

B- "An good" is incorrect because the indefinite article "an" is used before words starting with a vowel sound. "Good" starts with a consonant sound, so the definite article "a" should be used instead.

D- Both "an good" and "an healthy" are incorrect for the reasons mentioned above.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A. An engineer found a brilliant solution for the complex problem they encountered yesterday.

B. The engineer found a brilliant solution to the complex problem they encountered yesterday.

C. A engineer found a brilliant solution of the complex problem they encountered yesterday.

D. The engineer found a brilliant solution of the complex problem they encountered yesterday.
options: A
B
C
D
questions.solution:
Sentence B correctly uses the collocation "solution to" and the article "an" appropriately. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

A & D- The phrase "solution for/of" is incorrect. The correct collocation is "solution to."

C- "A engineer" is grammatically incorrect as "a" is used before the noun starting with a consonant sound, but "engineer" starts with a vowel sound. So, it should be "an engineer."

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A. I need to do homework before going out to meet my friends.

B. I need to have homework before going out to meet my friends.

C. I need to done homework before going out to meet my friends.

D. I need to do homework before going out to meet mine friends.
options: A
D
B
C
questions.solution:
Sentence A correctly uses the phrase "do homework" and is grammatically correct. The phrase "do homework" is appropriate for expressing the need to complete tasks. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

B- The phrase "have homework" suggests possessing or being assigned homework, rather than completing it, which is incorrect meaningfully.

C- The phrase "to done" is incorrect. The correct form should be "to do", as the infinitive marker "to" should be followed by the base verb ['Done' is V2/V3].

D- The possessive pronoun "mine" is used without a following noun. Here, since the noun follows it, it should be replaced with "my" (possessive determiner).

Note: Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

Possessive Pronouns: The pronouns mine, yours, hers, his, ours, and theirs are known as possessive pronouns: they refer to something owned by the speaker or by someone or something previously mentioned. For example: The pen is mine.

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

questions.question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition-
options: I have been working from home since last year.
I have been working from home from last year.
I have been working from home for last year.
I have been working from home to last year.
questions.solution:
Prepositions from, since, and for are used with reference to time.

From and since indicate a point of time while for indicates a period of time.

'To' is used to indicate a range or period of time.

Examples: The show will run from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. She has not spoken to him since last year. I have not met her for 10 years now. It takes five to ten minutes to finish

So, as per the rule, the correct sentence is - I have been working from home since last year.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.question:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the sentence that is error free from the given options.

No sooner when we planned the meeting, she arrived.
options: No sooner while we planned the meeting, she arrived.
No sooner than we planned the meeting, she arrived.
No sooner then we planned the meeting, she arrived.
No sooner as we planned the meeting, she arrived.
questions.solution:
In the given sentence, the format 'no sooner' should be always followed by 'than' and not the pronoun 'when'. Accordingly, only option (b), 'No sooner than we planned the meeting, she arrived' has the afore-mentioned word 'than' and so, only it can replace the given incorrect sentence and rest all are also incorrect.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: A better work-life balance are being demanding by employees.
A better work-life balance is demanding by employees.
A better work-life balance is being demanded by employees.
A better work-life balance are been demanded by employees.
questions.solution:
Options a) and d) are incorrect as they use the plural verb 'are' for the singular subject 'work-life balance'. It is a violation of the subject-verb agreement.

'Is demanding' is the construct for the active voice, but in the given sentence in option b), 'work-life balance' is the receiver of the action, so the passive voice construct should have been used here. So, option b) is incorrect too.

Option (c) is both grammatically and contextually correct.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

questions.question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of prepositions.
options: The team will travel to Amsterdam on 5<sup>th</sup> December.
The team will travel to Amsterdam in 5<sup>th</sup> December.
The team will travel to Amsterdam to 5<sup>th</sup> December.
The team will travel to Amsterdam of 5<sup>th</sup> December.
questions.solution: The preposition which is used while mentioning 'at the date of' is 'on'. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of adverb of frequency.
options: I drank coffee yesterday to start my day.
I drink coffee daily to start my day.
I don't like coffee on any day.
I drink coffee during my office hours.
questions.solution:
The sentence in option (b) is the sentence with the appropriate use of adverb of frequency.

'Daily' is an adverb of frequency which means 'happening on or relating to every day'.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

Adverb of Frequency: It tells us how often an action is performed.

Examples: always, never, frequently, often, etc.
